complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: Database Query Functions with Cursor Pagination
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Break down query implementation into: (1) Create app/lib/db/queries.ts with insertFurigana() function that computes rawTextSnippet as rawText.slice(0, 30) and validates input via FuriganaInsertSchema before INSERT; (2) Implement getFuriganaById(id) with WHERE id = :id AND deleted_at IS NULL clause returning FuriganaRow | null; (3) Implement listFuriganas() first-page query (no cursor) with ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC LIMIT :limit + 1; (4) Implement listFuriganas() cursor-based query using row-value comparison WHERE (created_at, id) < (:cursorCreatedAt, :cursorId) AND deleted_at IS NULL with proper base64 cursor encoding/decoding and CursorSchema validation; (5) Write comprehensive unit tests with in-memory SQLite (':memory:') covering pagination edge cases (first page, subsequent pages, last page detection via +1 fetch), cursor stability across concurrent inserts, soft-delete filtering, and nextCursor/hasMore correctness
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: High complexity. Row-value comparison for cursor pagination is tricky—requires understanding of database tuple comparison semantics and proper column ordering matching the index. Cursor encoding/decoding (base64) with Zod validation adds complexity. The +1 fetch strategy for hasMore detection requires careful array slicing. Soft-delete filtering must be consistent across all queries. Cursor stability testing (ensuring new inserts don't affect ongoing pagination) is non-trivial. In-memory SQLite testing infrastructure needs setup. Error handling for malformed cursors.

complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Break down into: (1) Create app/lib/sanitize.ts with sanitizeRawText() that strips HTML tags (/(<([^>]+)>)/gi), removes C0/C1 control characters (U+0000-U+001F except tab/newline/CR, U+007F, U+0080-U+009F) and BiDi overrides (U+200E, U+200F, U+202A-U+202E, U+2066-U+2069), normalizes whitespace (collapse consecutive spaces, preserve paragraph breaks), and trims; (2) Create app/lib/rate-limit.ts with in-memory Map<string, { count: number; resetAt: number }> rate limiter (10 req/60s per IP), extracting IP from x-forwarded-for header with fallback to 'unknown', and 60-second cleanup interval; (3) Write comprehensive unit tests for sanitization (HTML stripping, control character removal, BiDi override removal, whitespace normalization, Japanese text preservation) and rate limiter (under-limit allowance, over-limit blocking, time window reset, independent IP tracking)

Sanitization is more complex than existing sanitizeUserInput() in the codebase—requires Unicode range handling for control characters and BiDi overrides, careful whitespace normalization preserving paragraph breaks (double newlines). Both components are standalone utilities with clear requirements and good test coverage requirements.
